Date : 08.10.2024 Heard Mr. F. K. R. Ahmed, learned counsel for the petitioners.

Also heard Mr. D.
P. Goswami, learned APP appearing for the State.
By this application under section 482 BNSS, 2023, the petitioners are seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with Lanka P.S. Case No. 225/2024.
Let the case diary be produced on 04.11.2024.
The prayer for interim is opposed by the learned APP.

The allegation in the FIR is that the petitioner Nos. 1, 2 and 3, who are accused Nos. 4, 3 and 1 respectively in the FIR dated 15.07.2024 had resorted to dubious means and used forged Voter IDs and other documents to gain employment in CAPF.

However, on considering that in the police verification report issued by the Superintendent of Police, DSB, Hojai dated 06.06.2024, nothing adverse criminal report is available against them, the Court is inclined to grant interim pre-arrest bail to the petitioners namely, Gopal Mohan Mishra, Rajit Kumar and Abhishek Kumar by providing that in the event on their arrest in connection with Lanka P.S Case No.225/2024 [under Sections 468/420/471/120(B) IPC as per order dated 24.07.2024, passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Hojai], the petitioners shall be released on interim bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- each with one solvent surety of like amount Page No.# 3/3 to the satisfaction of the arresting officer.

The interim pre-arrest bail is granted on the following conditions:
1.
The petitioners shall appear before the I/O within 7(seven) days from the date of the order and shall cooperate with the investigation.
2. That the petitioners shall make themselves available to the police or any other investigating agency or Court in the present case as and when required.

3. That the petitioners shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him Page No.# 1/3 vs The State Of Assam on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12150014/
2 from disclosing such facts to Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
They shall not, in any manner, try to overawe or influence or intimidate the prosecution witness.
4. That the petitioners shall not obstruct the smooth progress of the investigation/trial.
5. That the petitioners shall not misuse their liberty in any manner.
6. That the petitioners shall not jump over the bail.
